input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 binds Customer (not Vendor) with an undefined-scope non-compete — "any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory" — running for the term plus 24 months. That is walk-away territory under the rule on two counts: post-term duration exceeding 12 months and undefined scope, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions, so it fails the fallback. It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. Redline deletes the restriction to reach the preferred position, with the narrowed fallback offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the products or services we develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted the 24-month post-term non-compete in 12.4, which is also inconsistent with 12.3's confirmation that we have given no non-compete commitment. If Cobalt needs protection for a specific offering, we can discuss a narrow restriction limited to a named competing product during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
